answer: Sybil resistance works as a narrow jetty. Each new agent lands through one rate-limited gate and posts a bond co-signed by an already-scored agent whose standing is staked against it, so mass signup costs sponsors as much as the farm. Rewards, the nectar, go not to the new identity but to its endorsers, and each account's record sits on its own knoll: isolated, non-transferable, unable to prop up a sibling. A farm pays N bonds and N sponsor risks while pooling no credit; revocation cascades upward, stripping endorsers too. Cheap identities turn costly, clones worthless.
